items.claim: 10:28's outcome antithesis (the righteous' prospect is joy / the wicked's hope perishes) is a self-contained bicolon correctly separated from 10:27's lifespan topic and 10:29's fortress-and-way-of-Yahweh topic.
items.evidence: Both quoted cola collate at skeleton tier to oshb:Prov.10.28 and match no other verse's vocabulary in the immediate span; the only lexical overlap with a neighbor is רשעים (wicked), shared with 10:27, but that noun recurs in nearly every antithetic verse of this chapter (book-wide antithetic-texture staging signal) and is not a distinguishing catchword.

items.claim: 10:30's land-tenure antithesis (the righteous never removed / the wicked not dwelling in the land) is correctly bounded between 10:29's fortress imagery and 10:31's speech-organ imagery, with no shared vocabulary crossing either seam.
items.evidence: Both quoted cola collate at skeleton tier to oshb:Prov.10.30; the only shared token with 10:31 is צדיק (righteous), the same generic righteous/wicked-class noun that recurs across nearly every verse of the antithetic run and carries no independent cohesion weight on its own.

items.claim: The cluster's core sweep evidence for 10:31-10:32 holds, but the row's assertion that "10:31 and 10:32 both end on" the noun תהפכות is byte-false for 10:31: its actual final word is the verb תכרת, with תהפכות sitting as the construct-chain noun before it (word 6 of 7), while 10:32 genuinely does end on תהפכות.
items.evidence: Word-split of the two verses' consonantal skeletons gives 10:31 = פי / צדיק / ינוב / חכמה / ולשון / תהפכות / תכרת (final word תכרת) versus 10:32 = שפתי / צדיק / ידעון / רצון / ופי / רשעים / תהפכות (final word תהפכות); an independent skeleton sweep of תהפכות returns exactly 9 verses book-wide (Prov.2.12, 2.14, 6.14, 8.13, 10.31, 10.32, 16.28, 16.30, 23.33) with 10:31-10:32 the sweep's only adjacent pair, and the opener parallel פי צדיק (10:31) / שפתי צדיק (10:32) is byte-confirmed at verse-initial position -- so the cluster's headline cohesion argument survives, but the specific 'both end on' wording overstates the parallel and should name תהפכות as 10:31's penultimate/construct-medial noun, not its closing word.

items.claim: 11:1's commerce-scale antithesis (false balance as YHWH's abomination / accurate weight as his delight) is correctly separated from 10:32's speech-organ close and 11:2's pride/humility topic.
items.evidence: Both quoted cola collate at skeleton tier to oshb:Prov.11.1; the one cross-boundary lexical echo -- רצון closing 10:32 versus the suffixed רצונו closing 11:1 -- is not a byte-identical shared token (a book-wide skeleton sweep of the bare form רצון returns 8 verses and does not include 11:1, because the suffixed form's medial nun+vav differs from the bare form's final-nun spelling) and carries a different referent in each verse (general approval in 10:32 versus YHWH's own pleasure in 11:1), so it does not contest the row's boundary.

items.claim: The cluster's headline evidence for 11:5-11:6 -- both verses opening on the construct צדקת, a skeleton sweep for which returns exactly these two verses book-wide -- is verified and strong, but the row's claim that both verses share "a verb ... with a third-person-plural object suffix" is byte-false for 11:5.
items.evidence: 11:5 = צדקת / תמים / תישר / דרכו / וברשעתו / יפל / רשע: the guidance verb תישר takes no pronominal suffix at all -- its object is the separate noun דרכו ('his way'), which itself carries a third-person SINGULAR suffix agreeing with the singular referent תמים ('the blameless one'); only 11:6's deliverance verb תצילם carries a genuine third-person-plural verb suffix, agreeing with the plural referent ישרים ('the upright ones'). The two verses share the rare construct opener and the antithetic virtue/vice template, but not a uniform suffix-person-and-number construction as claimed.

items.claim: 11:7's death/hope couplet is correctly read as a synthetic (not antithetic) pair narrating a single event, properly bounded between 11:6's virtue-construct sentence and 11:8's substitution image.
items.evidence: The quoted first colon collates at skeleton tier to oshb:Prov.11.7, and the connecting vav is non-adversative (both cola describe the wicked man's death), matching the row's own 'synthetic' device_notes call; the row's rationale paraphrases the second colon ('expectation of power') from the WEB rendering without quoting its Hebrew (אונים), a minor engagement gap, but the MT's own plene pointing of that word (vocalized with cholam, the 'vigor/might' root rather than the homographic 'iniquity' root) supports the WEB sense used, so the paraphrase is not translation-drift.

items.claim: 11:8's separation from 11:9 omits a book-unique shared verbal root: the deliverance root חלץ occurs in niphal in 11:8 (נחלץ) and in 11:9 (יחלצו) and NOWHERE else across all 915 verses of Proverbs, directly straddling the row's own claimed boundary.
items.evidence: A skeleton sweep for the final-tsade spelling חלץ returns only Prov.11.8, and a sweep for the medial-tsade spelling (needed because 11:9's יחלצו is not word-final) returns only Prov.11.9 -- together the root's total book-wide footprint is these two adjacent verses only, an even rarer footprint than the sweeps (9 and 2 verses respectively) the writer treats as decisive cluster evidence for the two proverb_cluster rows in this same batch (10:31-10:32, 11:5-11:6); the row's rationale never discloses this rival evidence for its 'substitution' vs. 'mouth/knowledge' topic-separation claim.

items.claim: 11:9's separation from 11:8 omits the same book-unique shared verbal root noted at 11:8: the deliverance root חלץ (niphal יחלצו here, נחלץ in 11:8) occurs ONLY in these two adjacent verses across all 915 verses of Proverbs.
items.evidence: The final-tsade skeleton sweep for חלץ returns only Prov.11.8 and the medial-tsade sweep (required because 11:9's form is non-word-final) returns only Prov.11.9; combined, the root is exclusive to this adjacent pair, a rarer footprint than either sweep result (9 verses, 2 verses) the writer relies on as decisive cluster evidence elsewhere in this same batch, yet the row's 'mouth/knowledge' framing does not disclose or rule out this rival cohesion evidence with its neighbor.
